project.title: Neuropeptidomics of the cockroach Rhyparobia maderae to characterize the neuropeptide landscape of the cockroach's circadian clock
project.projectDescription: The circadian clock of Rhyparobia maderae is the accessory medulla (AME) in the optic lobes of the brain. Controlled by compound ocular photoreceptors, the cockroach clock orchestrates circadian rhythms in physiology and behavior synchronized with environmental light-dark cycles. Approximately 240 neurons, rich in partially co-localized neuropeptides innervate the AME. Since the identity and function of most of these neuropeptides are unknown in the cockroach, we identify the neuropeptidome, a combination of analyses of brain/retrocerebral complex and AME extracts by Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometry (MS).
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Each sample set was collected in a 30 μl extraction solution containing 50% methanol, 49% H₂O and 1% formic acid (FA) on ice. The tissue samples were homogenized,centrifuged and desalted using self-packed Stage Tip C18 (IVA Analysentechnik e.K., Meerbusch, Germany) spin columns39. For analysis, peptides were separated on an EASY nanoLC 1000 UPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) coupled to a Q-Exactive Plus (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany) mass spectrometer.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data were analyzed with PEAKS Studio 10.5 (BSI, ON, Canada)with tolerance of 0.1 Da and fragment mass error tolerance of 0.05 Da. Only predicted peptides with a minimum amino acid length of five amino acid residues, a maximum molecular weight of 10 kDa and a P-score > 60 were considered. with tolerance of 0.1 Da and fragment mass error tolerance of 0.05 Da.
